vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: A detailed technical description of a material or a piece of equipment
The amount of water that passes a point in a period of time
The work of keeping equipment in good condition
To say officially that something is good enough
The list of what is and is not included in a project
The maximum amount that a system can take
A building with pumps that move water or sewage to a higher place
Something that a project must have or do

vocab.text: Capacity and flow rate are not the same thing. The flow rate is what passes through the plant at this moment; the capacity is the most it can ever take. A plant designed for six hundred liters per second can run for years at four hundred, and that difference is exactly what a scope has to protect.

reading.rtitle: Scope of Work: Treatment Plant Upgrade (Sections 2 and 3)
paras: Section 2 describes what is included in the project. The existing treatment plant is operated by the city water utility and serves about one hundred and eighty thousand people. Under this contract, its capacity is increased from four hundred to six hundred liters per second, and two new pumping stations are built on the east side of the city. All the equipment is described in Annex B, and every requirement in that annex is considered mandatory. Only the specification is fixed: the brand of each piece of equipment is chosen by the contractor.

Section 3 describes how the work is controlled. The design is prepared by the consultancy and approved by the utility before any construction starts. During operation, the flow rate is measured every hour, and the results are sent to the client every month. After delivery, maintenance is not included in this contract: it is done by the utility's own team, which is trained by the contractor during the last month of the project.

reading.prompt: What is the main purpose of these two sections?
choices: To sell the pumps of one specific brand
To say what the project includes and how the work is controlled and approved
To explain how sewage is treated by bacteria

items: The existing plant is operated by the consultancy.
The text says the plant is operated by the city water utility.
The design must be approved before construction starts.
The text says the design is approved by the utility before any construction starts.
Maintenance after delivery is part of this contract.
The text says maintenance is not included: it is done by the utility's own team.
A new engineer asks who does the maintenance after delivery. Explain, with the passive.
The contractor wants to use a different brand of pump. Explain what is fixed and what is not.
Karen asks how the client knows the plant is working. Explain how the results are measured and sent.

practice.title: Rewrite each sentence in the passive. Keep by only when it matters.
items: The team measures the flow rate every hour.
We send the results every month.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: The plant is operated by the utility.
The flow rate is measured every hour.
The brand is chosen by the contractor.
The results are sent every month.
answerkey.note: These are models, not the only correct answers. Any natural passive with is or are and the right participle works.

items.situation: Karen asks who operates the plant today. It is the city water utility.
tips: Start with the plant, not with the utility.

items.situation: A colleague asks how often the flow rate is checked. The answer is every hour.
tips: Nobody cares who checks it: the passive.
The flow rate is ... every hour.

items.situation: The client asks whether maintenance is part of the contract. It is not.
tips: Negative passive: isn't plus the participle.
Say who does it instead, with by.

items.situation: Somebody asks where the details of the pumps are. They are in Annex B.
tips: Use the word for a detailed technical description.

items.situation: Ask the client whether the design has to be accepted before construction.
tips: Passive question: Is plus subject plus participle.
Use the verb that means to accept officially.

listenings.text: Welcome to the North River treatment plant. Before we start the tour, a few rules. Helmets and boots are required in every area after this door. The sewage arrives here from the whole east side of the city, and first it is screened to remove the solids. Then the water is sent to these large tanks, where it is treated by bacteria for about eight hours. Samples are taken every two hours and tested in the lab next door. Photos are allowed, but please do not touch any valve. The tour takes about forty minutes.

Hi Thiago, it is Paul from the utility, with a quick note on how the design review works on our side. Every design is checked by two engineers, and the comments are sent back to you within ten days. Small changes are accepted by email, but a new drawing is required for any change in capacity. Nothing is approved on Fridays, so please do not send anything important that day. Call me if anything is unclear. Thanks.

extra_audio.text: First, the scope is written and sent to the consultancy. Then, the design is prepared by the consultancy. After that, the design is approved by the utility. Next, the pumping stations are built and the capacity is increased. Finally, the flow rate is measured every hour and the results are sent to the client.
